## PM claim + dispatch order — R27

Claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Branch: `claude/issue-6171-report-schema-name`.

### Ruling: take the card's own suggested resolution. **Rename the subject to `ReportComponentSchema`. No source change.**

This needs no contract decision, which is what separates it from its siblings (#6169, #6172's collision half, #6155 — all escalated or held). Three facts settle it without anyone choosing anything:

1. **The page's own example fence already imports `ReportComponentSchema`.** The prose disagrees with the code on the same page.
2. **PR #6168 already named this page's property tables `ReportComponentSchema`.** The convention is set and landed; the title and H1 are simply the parts that sweep did not touch.
3. **`ReportComponentSchema` is what actually exists** (`packages/types/src/reports.ts:354`), and all four rows of the Basic Configuration table are members of it.

So the rename makes the page self-consistent and consistent with a landed precedent. ⛔ Do not propose renaming the *type* — the source is right and the prose is wrong.

### ⚠️ Why this is worse than a typo, and why the fix must not be a blind find-and-replace

`ReportSchema` **is a real exported name** — `@objectstack/spec` uses it for the dataset-bound report shape in `json-schema/ui/Report.json` (`name` / `label` / `dataset` / `rows` / `columns` / `values`). That is a **different shape**, and it is the one `content/docs/plugins/plugin-report.mdx` documents.

So a reader following the name today lands on a real, wrong declaration rather than on nothing — which is the harder failure to notice. And it means:

⛔ **Do not rename occurrences of `ReportSchema` outside `content/docs/core/report-schema.mdx`.** On `plugin-report.mdx` the name is **correct** and must stay. Scope the edit to the one page, and confirm by measurement that you have not touched the other.

### What to change on that page

The card names three sites; verify the set rather than trusting the count:

- frontmatter `title: "Report Schema (ReportSchema)"`
- the H1 lead sentence
- any other prose reference on that page

**Enumerate every occurrence on that page first and report the number**, then confirm zero remain after the edit. If the page's own example fence or tables already say `ReportComponentSchema`, leave them exactly as they are — PR #6168 landed those and re-touching them would put this diff on top of a sweep for no reason.

### Verification

- Re-measure before editing: confirm `ReportSchema` still resolves to nothing in this tree (not in `@object-ui/types`' built `.d.ts`, not in `packages/*/src`) and that `ReportComponentSchema` does resolve. ⭐ **Both readings, not just the first** — an empty grep with no positive control is not a reading, and this card's whole subject is a name that resolves somewhere unexpected.
- Confirm `@objectstack/spec` still exports `ReportSchema` for the other shape, so the "one name, two shapes" hazard is stated from a live reading rather than inherited from this card.
- Gate union with exit codes captured by redirect **before** any pipe, each quoting its own verdict line: `check:doc-snippet-types`, `check:doc-types`, `docs:check-links`, `check:control-bytes`.
- **Derive each gate's scope from its own configuration** rather than assuming which apply, and measure any exclusion instead of asserting it.
- Root vitest only, per objectui#3378 — never package-scoped.
- Changeset per the presence gate's own verdict. objectui has no `skip-changeset` mechanism, so that verdict is the declaration form.

### Scope

`content/docs/core/report-schema.mdx` only. ⛔ Not `plugin-report.mdx`. ⛔ No source change. ⛔ Not #6121's subject — that card covers this same page's *authoring examples* contradicting their types (`dataSource`, `exports`) and is `needs-user-decision`; it is a different sentence set and is not yours. If you find the two overlapping in the same lines, stop and say so rather than deciding it.

⚠️ This page is also in #5867's `core` group (11 blocks / 1 file), currently blocked on #6121. Your diff is prose and frontmatter, not fences, so it should not collide — but note in your PR body that the page has in-flight interest, per the repo's shared-surface guidance.

## PM review — ACCEPTED. PR #6192 armed. ⭐ The card's premise was half false, and the correction makes the ruling *stronger*.

Reviewed against a pinned ref. All 21 checks green, 0 failures.

### The measurement I asked for found more than the card listed

The card named three sites. There are **four** — the frontmatter title (L2), the H1 lead (L10), plus *"ReportSchema provides:"* (L14) and *"ReportSchema is perfect for:"* (L458), neither of which the card's explicit list named.

This is why the order said **verify the set, do not trust the count**. Re-derived myself against `main`:

| reading | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bare `ReportSchema` on the page | **4** | **0** |
| `ReportComponentSchema` on the page | 8 | **12** |
| diff | — | 4 files… no: **1 file, +4 / −4** |

The 8 pre-existing `ReportComponentSchema` occurrences are byte-identical — PR #6168 landed those and they were not re-touched, as ordered.

⭐ And my explicit negative control holds: `content/docs/plugins/plugin-report.mdx` hashes **identically** before and after (`6003c22e…`), with its one **correct** `ReportSchema` occurrence intact. That was the thing a blind find-and-replace would have destroyed, and it is now proven untouched by sha rather than by assertion.

### ⭐ The premise correction is the best part of this round

The card said `ReportSchema` *"resolves to nothing in this tree — not in `@object-ui/types`' built `.d.ts`, **not in `packages/*/src`**"*. **The second half is false**: it appears 15 times in `packages/*/src`, imported from `@objectstack/spec/ui` by app-shell metadata-admin and plugin-report.

The dev could have quietly relied on the card and shipped the same diff. Instead they measured, found the card wrong, and reported it — and what they found makes the ruling **better founded than I knew when I made it**:

> `packages/types/src/spec-report.ts:103` deliberately re-exports the spec symbol as **`SpecReportSchema`**, under the comment *"Spec\* prefix to avoid collision with legacy reports.ts"*.

⭐ **The repo had already renamed around this exact collision — everywhere except this page's prose.** So this is not a fresh naming judgement at all; it is the last unswept instance of a convention the codebase already adopted. That is a much stronger basis than "the page's own example fence disagrees with its title", which is what I ruled on.

Both readings were taken with a positive control, as ordered: bare `ReportSchema` in the built `.d.ts` = 0 files; `ReportComponentSchema` = 5 files, declared at `packages/types/dist/reports.d.ts:289`. (Source line is `reports.ts:359`, not the `:354` the card gave — another inherited number that had moved.)

The `@objectstack/spec` hazard was confirmed **live** rather than inherited: 17.2.0 does export `ReportSchema`, and `Report.json` measures as the dataset-bound shape `plugin-report.mdx` documents.

### No collision with #6121

Verified rather than assumed: #6121's subject lines are inside fences and the property table (L88, L231); this diff is L2 / L10 / L14 / L458. Disjoint, so the `core` group's eventual unblocking is unaffected.

### Two process notes I am taking on the chin

1. **My order named `check:doc-snippet-types` again** — the script *file*, not the npm script (`check:doc-snippets`). Second card in a row where a dev had to correct that. It is now in objectstack#11901's territory as a recurring PM-side defect, not a one-off.
2. ⭐ The dev derived `check:doc-fences` from the gates' own config even though my list omitted it — and its #5867 ratchet reading is **unmoved**, since no fence changed. That is the check that would have caught a rename accidentally touching a fenced block.

⭐ And one reading worth carrying to every doc card: `check:doc-snippets` **first ran exit=1** with *"The snippet program was NOT run: the packages it resolves against are not built"*. Correctly diagnosed as an unbuilt tree, rebuilt, re-run green — and recorded, because **an unbuilt-tree exit is indistinguishable from a real failure at the exit-code level.** A dev who trusted the first exit code would have reported a false red; one who trusted a cached green would have reported a false pass.

The vitest narrowing was declared as a measurement rather than a claim: population read from `vitest list --filesOnly` (1971 files), 0 of which reference this page, and `content/docs` appears 0 times in the config so no project can pick up an `.mdx` under it.
